body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyānasūtra</s> (Great Vehicle Discourse) called <s>Āryapratītyasamutpāda</s> (Noble Dependent Origination).

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān trāyastriṃśānāṃ devānāṃ madhye viharati sma pāṇḍukambalakalpe śilātale jitāśvādimahāśrāvakaiḥ āryamaitreyāvalokiteśvaravajrahastādibhirbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ aprameyaguṇaratnālaṃkṛtaiḥ mahābrahmasahāṃpatinārāyaṇamaheśvarādibhirdevaiḥ śakreṇa devānāmindreṇa gandharvarājena pañcaśikhena ca sārdham | athāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ utthāyāsanāt ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānuṃ merupṛṣṭhe 'vaṣṭabhya yena bhaganān tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - ete hi bhagavan devāḥ caityanamaskriyāmaṇḍanāḥ etatpariṣanmaṇḍalapatitāḥ kathamapi brahmacaryapuṇyaprasavāḥ sadevake samārake sabrahmake loke saśramaṇabrāhmaṇaprajāsu bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇyaḥ upāsakopāsikāḥ subahulapuṇyaprasavāḥ bhagavato dharmadeśanāṃ yācante iti | tadā bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ pratītyasamutpādagāthāmavocat -
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling among the gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) heaven, upon the stone surface of <s>Pāṇḍukambala</s> (the white lotus stone throne), together with great <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) such as <s>Jitāśva</s> and others, with <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> (great beings) such as the noble <s>Maitreya</s>, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, <s>Vajrahasta</s>, and others, adorned with immeasurable qualities and jewels, with gods such as great <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, and others, with <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods (<s>Indra</s>), and with <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, king of the <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians). Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, pressed his right knee upon the surface of <s>Meru</s> (the cosmic mountain), joined his palms in reverence toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, these gods who have come adorned with worship of <s>caityas</s> (sacred shrines), who have fallen into this assembly circle, who have in some measure generated merit through the holy life — in this world with its gods, <s>Māras</s>, and <s>Brahmās</s>, among the people including <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (brahmins), the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), <s>upāsakas</s> (male lay followers), and <s>upāsikās</s> (female lay followers) who have generated exceedingly abundant merit — they all request the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> (doctrine)." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke to them the verse on <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination):

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat |
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) that arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One) has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that which is their cessation — thus has spoken the great <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic).

body.text: yadidamavalokiteśvara ayaṃ pratītyasamutpādastathāgatānāṃ dharmakāyaḥ | yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyati, sa tathāgataṃ paśyati | yaśca avalokiteśvara kulaputraḥ kuladuhitā vā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ apratiṣṭhite pṛthivīpradeśe āmalakamātraṃ caityaṃ sūcīmātraṃ bodhivṛkṣaṃ bakulapuṣpamātraṃ chatraṃ kṛtvā pratītyasamutpādadharmadhātugāthāṃ paṭhati, sa brāhmaṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati | itaḥ pracyāvya maraṇakālaṃ kṛtvā brahmaloke utpadyate | tataḥ pracyāvya kālaṃ kṛtvā śuddhāvāsakāyikānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyāmutpadyate ||
body.translated_text: O <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, this <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) is the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> (Thus-Gone Ones). Whoever sees <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> sees the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And, O <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, whatever son or daughter of good family, endowed with faith, in an uninhabited tract of land, having erected a <s>caitya</s> (sacred shrine) the size of an <s>āmalaka</s> (myrobalan fruit), a <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s> (bodhi tree) the size of a needle, and an umbrella the size of a <s>bakula</s> flower, and recites the verse on <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> and <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of truth), that person generates <s>brāhma</s> (divine) merit. Having departed from this [world], at the time of death, that person is born in the <s>Brahmaloka</s> (world of Brahmā). Having departed from there at the time of death, that person is born in the company of the gods of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes).

body.text: evamavocadbhagavān | sa rve ca te śrāvakāḥ, te ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, sarvāvatī ca sā parṣat, sadevamanuṣyāsuragandharvalokaśca bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One). And all those <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> (great beings), and that entire assembly, and the world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s> (titans), and <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians) rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
The <s>Mahāyānasūtra</s> (Great Vehicle Discourse) called <s>Āryapratītyasamutpāda</s> (Noble Dependent Origination) is complete.
